newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian court told religious leaders killed.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian court told religious leaders killed.

text.p: Witnesses in the trial of Ethiopia's former Marxist leaders on Tuesday told how two religious leaders were tortured and finally killed.

The witnesses, who under court rules cannot be named, said His Holiness Abuna Tewoflos, second patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church and Kess Gudina Tumsa, secretary-general of the Ethiopian Mekane Yesus Evangelical Church, were both executed during the rule of Mengistu Haile Mariam.
Ethiopias new government has charged 5,198 people suspected of involvement in the "Red Terror" campaign during the 17-year Marxist rule of Mengistu, but most are yet to appear in court.
Mengistu was ousted by rebels in 1991 and now lives in exile in Zimbabwe.
The first witness, a former vice minister, spent over seven years in prison for being an opponent of Mengistu's military junta commonly known as the Dergue.

"We learnt that His Holiness Abuna Tewoflos, Patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church who was taken out of jail by armed guards, was executed by the Dergue after being subjected to torture," the first witness told the court.
The second witness, the 60-year-old widow of Kess Gudina told the court that her husband was subjected to humiliation and later killed on orders of the Dergue.

"Kess Gudina, secretary-general of the Ethiopian Mekane Yesus Evangelical Church, was subjected to humiliation and was later killed by the Dergue," said the wife, herself imprisoned for 10 years by Mengistu's government.
Death squads in a terror campaign in 1977 and 1978 hunted down thousands of people from rival Marxist groups and other opposition organisations on behalf of the Dergue.
Only 46 out of 71 former Dergue officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity are on trial, the 25 others including Mengistu are being tried in absentia.
All 71 could be sentenced to death if found guilty. Mengistu ruled from 1977 until May 1991 when he fled the country shortly before rebels entered the capital.

The former vice minister told the court that Abuna was brought to a cell in prison where Emperor Haile Selassie's top officials had been jailed by the Dergue in 1974 and tied to a makeshift bed before his execution.
"His Holiness was put in death cell number three. His hands and legs were tied to a makshfit bed inside cell number three and his official robe was taken off him," he said.
"In front of all of us in cell number one, the late patriarch accused the Dergue of being enemies of the Ethiopian people, bent on destroying its history and culture," he said.
The patriarch fasted without food and water for 45 days. "He prayed day and night non-stop," he added.
The witness said the religious leader was later taken away by armed guards and never returned.
"We later learnt that the Dergue executed him along with other officials and their bodies was buried in a compound on the outskirts of Addis Ababa," the witness added.
The elderly wife of Kess Gudina told the court that Dergue security men blocked the Mekane Yesus Church in Addis Ababa in 1979 and abducted her husband from a car she was driving.
With tears rolling down her face, the widow said she had not seen her husband since his abduction and only learnt about his death in 1991.
The remains of the two religious leaders were exhumed and accorded a Christian funeral after their burial place was identified by a former soldier working under Mengistu.
The trial was adjourned until next week.
